checks.question: Was live highest-authority state refreshed immediately before planning/execution?
Is the action bound to the current canonical generation/commit and fail-closed on drift?
Is the terminal objective and current causal frontier explicit?
Is the default action a real consequential task that exercises a useful capability, rather than a synthetic proxy?
If this is supporting work, does one exact unresolved predicate currently block the selected real task and will this action directly resolve it?
Has the synthetic/support action budget since the last real-output event not been exceeded?
Can this action be traced to reusable capability inheritance, verified real-task completion, fresh reuse, frontier dependency removal, or residual-gap localization?
Does the action avoid assumptions contradicted by live canonical state?
Were inherited capabilities, artifacts, prior tasks, connected tools, software and equivalent routes searched before creation?
Have reuse/composition routes been preferred over adaptation/invention unless falsified or slower?
Was evidence state explicitly classified using the canonical evidence-presence classes?
If capability is proven but proof is missing, is evidence recovery used instead of rerun?
For missing evidence, were higher recovery steps exhausted first?
Is any new infrastructure strictly required because the current real task cannot produce correct capability output without it?
If freezing a held-out/hidden gate, were carrier, runtime contract, verifier, closure and orthogonality already generically proven without hidden payload?
Has this failure class occurred fewer than the allowed repeats without root-cause change?
Does verification close a material uncertainty that changes a capability decision?
If an adequate route exists, are we using it rather than continuing research/platform search?
If user action is requested, is it the smallest genuine external authority boundary?
